newsitem.title: QATAR: Qatar joins gas exporters club with first cargo.
newsitem.headline: Qatar joins gas exporters club with first cargo.

text.p: Qatar on Monday joined the exclusive league of international gas exporters as a customised liquefied natural gas (LNG) tanker left its Ras Laffan port for Japan.

The cargo, equivalent to 65,000 tonnes of LNG, is the first of 100 million tonnes of LNG contracted by Japan's Chubu Electric Power Company Inc under a sales-and-purchase agreement running over 25 years.

The gas was supplied by the Qatar Liquefied Gas Company Ltd (Qatargas) which is owned 65 percent owned by the Qatar government, 10 percent each by United States' Mobil Corp and France's Total SA and 7.5 percent each by Japan's Mitsui Corp and Marubeni Corp.

Qatar's Minister of Energy and Industry, Abdullah bin Hamad al-Attiyah, called it a "historic moment" as the Al Zubarah tanker left Ras Laffan for the Japanese port of Nagoya to discharge its cargo expectedly on January 10.
Another ship, the Al Khor, is expected to dock in early January to carry a second shipment.
Qatargas is the first of the oil and gas-rich Gulf Arab state's three major gas export projects designed to cash in on its massive gas reserves- the third largest in the world after Russia and Iran.
It is designed to produce six million tonnes annually of which four million tonnes a year s committed to Chubu and two million tonnes to seven other Japanese power and gas utilities.

The other projects are Ras Laffan LNG Company, or Rasgas, which aims to export 10 million tonnes a year eventually and Qatar-Enron LNG Marketing Company designed to produce five million tonnes annually.
Rasgas's first phase, expected to produce five million tonnes a year, is expected to go on stream in July 1999, and Qatar-Enron project in 2001.
